name: When should I repair my wood fence versus replacing it entirely?

mainEntity.name: When should I repair my wood fence versus replacing it entirely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repairing your wood fence is often a cost-effective solution if only a few posts, panels, or pickets are damaged, or if the overall structure remains sound. For instance, if you have localized rot near the ground on a few posts, spot repairs can extend the fence's life. However, if more than 20-30% of your fence shows signs of extensive rot, widespread structural instability, or significant insect damage, a full replacement might offer better long-term value. Our team at Maine Results, Inc. can assess the extent of the damage during an on-site visit in areas like Garden City or Meridian to help you make an informed decision based on your fence's condition and your budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider repair for localized damage, but replacement might be better for widespread rot or structural issues affecting over 20-30% of the fence. An on-site assessment can determine the best approach.
